newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil current acct gap to July at 4.35 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil current acct gap to July at 4.35 pct/GDP.

text.p: The deficit in Brazil's current account reached $33.449 billion, or 4.35 percent of gross domestic product, in the 12 months to July, the Central Bank said Monday.
The Central Bank said in a statement that the current account gap in the 12 months through June was 4.2 percent of GDP, and in the 12 months to July 1996 stood at 2.01 percent of GDP.
Brazil's foreign reserves in July rose to a net $59.493 billion from $56.795 billion the previous month, the bank said.
According to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable, July's reserves were $60.331 billion compared with $57.615 billion in June, it said.
The bank also said that net foreign direct investment in the seven months to July was $8.804 billion after inflows of $1.418 billion last month.
It said that in the whole of 1996 foreign direct investment was $9.889 billion.
The bank said foreign direct investment in the 12 months to July covered 47.3 percent of the current account deficit.
The Central Bank said that the services account of the balance of payments showed a $14.707 billion deficit in the January-July period.
Net payments on interest amounted to $5.533 billion.

The deficit on international travel, which includes what Brazilians spend abroad, was $2.501 billion in the seven-month period while the shortfall in the transport section of the services account was $2.397 billion.
